ledger.note: 1757: Najib-ud-daula takes Dehradun. Najib-ud-daula, governor of Saharanpur, "invaded in 1757 along with his Rohilla Army and captured Dehradun" (the page marks the sentence citation needed).

region.text: Garhwal: the part of Uttarakhand west of about 79.4 E, from the Dehra Dun valley to the Alaknanda and Mandakini

ledger.note: 14 May 1804: Pradyumna Shah is defeated and killed by the Gurkhas at Khurbura near Dehradun and Garhwal passes to them. The Pradyumna Shah page: "He reigned over Garhwal from 1785 to 14 May 1804, until his defeat to the Gurkha forces after the Battle of Khurbura occurred near Dehradun" and "the king died on 14 May 1804 while trying to save his kingdom". The Garhwal Kingdom page: infobox "Conquered by the Gorkhas and merged with the Kingdom of Nepal: 1804"; "The occupation of the kingdom by the Gorkhas went unopposed from 1803 to 1814"; it also has the dynasty ruling "until 1803" in one place and "up to 1804" in another. The Pradyumna page dates neither the invasion nor an occupation.

region.text: Tehri Garhwal: the Tehri Garhwal district and most of Uttarkashi district

ledger.note: 1815: the Gorkhas are driven out of Garhwal and Tehri Garhwal is restored under the British. The Sugauli page: Ochterlony pushed the Nepalese out of Garhwal and Kumaon "across the Kali River" in 1815, "ending a 12-year occupation"; the treaty was "signed on 4 March 1816" (drafted 2 December 1815) and is silent on Tehri, the Dun and the restoration of the Panwar line. The Garhwal Kingdom page: at the end of the war "the British annexed half of the Kingdom of Garhwal", which became Pauri Garhwal, and "the other half, Tehri Garhwal, became a subsidiary princely state"; its infobox has "Established as a Princely state of British India following the Treaty of Sugauli: 1816", and its text dates the treaty to 21 April 1815, which the Sugauli page contradicts. The year of the gain is the page's 1815 for the expulsion; the princely state dates from 1816. The Sudarshan Shah page is silent on 1815.

wars.outcome: Ochterlony pushed the Nepalese out of Garhwal and Kumaon in 1815; the Treaty of Sugauli, signed 4 March 1816, made the Kali the western boundary and the British annexed half of Garhwal (Pauri Garhwal) and restored the other half as Tehri Garhwal.
wars.note: Sugauli page: "Nepal ceded ... all the hill territories" west of the Kali (Article 5, undated in the sentence); signed 4 March 1816 between the East India Company and Nepal. The Garhwal Kingdom page dates the treaty to 21 April 1815, which the Sugauli page contradicts.

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary; the principalities and the Dun are regions.
The treaty division of 1815 and the princely state of Tehri Garhwal (10,800 km2 in 1901) are named administrative units; the drawn circles are approximate.

notes: Four pages opened (Garhwal Kingdom, Pradyumna Shah, Treaty of Sugauli, Sudarshan Shah). Contradictions on the page: founding 823 (infobox, text) against the table (Kanak Pal 688-699) and 888 for the Chandpur Garhi capital period; the capital dates (infobox) against the text (Devalgarh 1358, Srinagar after 1622, Narendranagar 1919); the end of the dynasty "until 1803" and "up to 1804"; the date of the Treaty of Sugauli (the Garhwal page says 21 April 1815; the Treaty of Sugauli page, opened, gives drafted 2 December 1815 and signed 4 March 1816, and the dossier follows the Sugauli page; the Gorkha ouster from Garhwal is 1815 on the Sugauli page, 1814 on the Garhwal page's "1803 to 1814"). Three more pages opened: Pradyumna Shah (14 May 1804 at Khurbura near Dehradun), Treaty of Sugauli and Sudarshan Shah (silent on 1815 and on territory). No page opened says what the British kept (Dehradun, Srinagar, eastern Garhwal) beyond the Garhwal page's "half". The nepal dossier already carries the matching gain of garhwal-kingdom in 1804 and the loss of Kumaon and the Far West to the British in April-May 1815; it names no separate 1815 loss of Garhwal. The Gorkha Kingdom Cliopatria row ends in 1787, so the counterpart here is nepal, not gorkha-kingdom. british-empire (sa-06) should record the vassal_start for tehri garhwal (garhwal-kingdom) from 1815 or 1816 to 1947. Gazetteer lacks Garhwal, Tehri, Uttarkashi, Chandpur Garhi as names; admin1 Uttarakhand plus a polygon cut and coordinate circles are used. Counterparts needing dossiers: Najib-ud-daula's Rohilla territory (Saharanpur and the Dun).
